software.name: QuickBooks Online
software.tagline: Intuit's cloud accounting, from a free plan to Advanced, with job costing and inventory from the Plus plan up
software.pricing_summary: Six plans at regular monthly prices (checked September 30, 2026): Free $0 (1 user, 2 invoices a month, 1 bank connection, no accountant access), Lite $20 (the plan on Intuit's QuickBooks Solopreneur page), Simple Start $38 (1 user plus 2 accountants), Essentials $85 (3 users), Plus $140 (5 users; adds project profitability and inventory) and Advanced $340 (25 users plus 3 accountants). Paid plans are offered with either a 30-day free trial or 50% off for 3 months; no annual contract, and Intuit says you can switch plans or cancel at any time. Intuit changed the prices of Essentials, Plus and Advanced for renewals on or after August 1, 2026, and says recent subscribers keep their price for the first six months; Free, Lite and Simple Start were unchanged.
software.long_description:
QuickBooks Online (QBO) is cloud accounting software from Intuit, a public company headquartered in Mountain View, California. Your bank and credit-card transactions sync in for categorizing, and QBO handles invoicing and payments, bills, expenses, receipt capture and mileage tracking in the mobile app, and financial reports. You can invite your accountant at no extra cost, and Intuit runs a ProAdvisor directory for finding independent accountants and bookkeepers certified in QuickBooks.

For a trades business, the draw is connections. Many field-service tools sync to QBO; Jobber, for example, says its integration works with the US and Global versions of QuickBooks Online, and Knowify syncs with both QuickBooks Online and Desktop. Six plans run from a limited Free plan and Lite ($20/mo) through Simple Start ($38), Essentials ($85), Plus ($140) and Advanced ($340) at regular monthly prices. Project profitability tracking and inventory start at Plus, and Advanced adds what Intuit calls a construction financials solution and advanced project financials.

Cost is the main thing to watch. Intuit changed the prices of Essentials, Plus and Advanced for renewals on or after August 1, 2026 (it says recent subscribers keep their price for the first six months of their subscription), and payroll costs extra: Intuit's payroll bundles start at $88/mo plus $6.50 per employee with Simple Start, against $38 for Simple Start alone.

The trade-off: QBO is broad and widely supported by field-service tools and bookkeepers, but the plan most contractors need for job costing (Plus) lists at $140/mo, users are capped by tier, and payroll is extra. Xero charges no per-user license fees, FreshBooks is built around invoicing and billing clients, and Wave has a free Starter plan; compare them if price or simplicity matters more than breadth.
software.how_it_works: You connect your bank and credit-card accounts, and transactions sync into QuickBooks for categorizing and reconciling. From there you send invoices and take payments, enter bills, snap receipts and track mileage in the mobile app, and run reports. Plus adds project profitability tracking, inventory and up to 40 classes and locations; Advanced adds construction financials, advanced project financials, workflow automation, unlimited classes and locations, and 25 users. Field-service tools such as Jobber sync customers and invoices into QBO so you don't enter them twice. Payroll is added through Intuit's payroll bundles. New subscribers see either a 30-day free trial or 50% off for 3 months on paid plans.

pros_detail.title: Wide field-service support
pros_detail.explanation: Many field-service tools sync with QuickBooks Online. Jobber says its integration works with the US and Global versions of QBO, and Knowify syncs with QuickBooks Online and Desktop. Check your own tool's integration page for what syncs and which plan you need.

pros_detail.title: Easy to find QuickBooks help
pros_detail.explanation: Intuit's ProAdvisor directory lets you search by location and industry for independent accountants and bookkeepers certified in QuickBooks, and paid plans include free accountant logins (2 on Simple Start through Plus, 3 on Advanced).

pros_detail.title: Room to grow
pros_detail.explanation: Plans run from a free tier to Advanced with 25 users, so you can move up as you add staff, inventory or more complex projects without switching software.

pros_detail.title: Job costing on Plus and up
pros_detail.explanation: Plus adds project profitability tracking and inventory; Advanced adds what Intuit calls a construction financials solution and advanced project financials for larger contractors.

pros_detail.title: Payroll from the same vendor
pros_detail.explanation: Intuit sells payroll bundled with QBO plans (Workforce Payroll + Simple Start lists at $88/mo plus $6.50 per employee), so books and payroll can live in one place.

cons_detail.title: Recent price change
cons_detail.explanation: Intuit changed Essentials, Plus and Advanced prices for renewals on or after August 1, 2026; they now list at $85, $140 and $340 a month. Free, Lite and Simple Start prices did not change.

cons_detail.title: Job costing needs Plus
cons_detail.explanation: Project profitability and inventory start at Plus ($140/mo list), so a contractor who needs job costing can't stay on the cheaper tiers.

cons_detail.title: Users capped by tier
cons_detail.explanation: Simple Start allows 1 user, Essentials 3, Plus 5 and Advanced 25, plus the free accountant logins. Xero, by contrast, charges no per-user license fees.

cons_detail.title: Payroll adds to the bill
cons_detail.explanation: Payroll is a separate cost: Intuit's Workforce Payroll + Simple Start bundle lists at $88/mo plus $6.50 per employee, against $38 for Simple Start alone.

cons_detail.title: Free plan is very limited
cons_detail.explanation: The Free plan allows 1 user, 2 invoices a month (more if you qualify for QuickBooks Payments), 1 bank connection and no accountant access, so most working businesses need a paid plan.

software.best_for: Trades businesses that want accounting their bookkeeper and field-service software already support, and that need job costing (Plus) or construction financials (Advanced)
software.weaknesses: Essentials, Plus and Advanced prices changed for renewals from August 1, 2026; job costing and inventory need Plus ($140/mo list); users capped by tier (1, 3, 5 or 25); payroll costs extra

ratings.reddit_sentiment: the default everyone integrates with; widely used but frequently criticized for relentless price increases

software.affiliate_payout_note: Intuit runs a QuickBooks affiliate program, but it's limited/curated; affiliate_url stays TBD until tracking is confirmed

faqs.q: How much does QuickBooks Online cost in 2026?
faqs.a: Regular monthly prices: Free $0 (1 user, 2 invoices a month), Lite $20, Simple Start $38 (1 user), Essentials $85 (3 users), Plus $140 (5 users) and Advanced $340 (25 users). New subscribers see either a 30-day free trial or 50% off for 3 months on paid plans, with no annual contract. Essentials, Plus and Advanced prices changed for renewals on or after August 1, 2026.

faqs.q: Will my field-service software sync with QuickBooks Online?
faqs.a: Many field-service tools offer a QuickBooks Online sync. Jobber says its integration works with all QuickBooks Online plans in the US and Global versions except QuickBooks Self-Employed, and Knowify syncs with both QuickBooks Online and Desktop. Check your own tool's integration page for what syncs and which of its plans includes the sync.

faqs.q: QuickBooks Online vs Xero for a trades business?
faqs.a: Both are full cloud accounting. QuickBooks caps users by plan (1 on Simple Start up to 25 on Advanced), while Xero charges no per-user license fees on its three US plans, which rise to $27, $59 and $97 a month on October 1, 2026. If your bookkeeper and field-service tool are set up for QuickBooks, QBO is the simpler choice; if you need many logins on a budget, price out Xero.

faqs.q: Which QuickBooks Online plan do trades need?
faqs.a: Solo operators can start on Lite ($20/mo) or Simple Start ($38/mo). If you need job costing (project profitability) or inventory, you need Plus ($140/mo). Advanced ($340/mo) adds construction financials, advanced project financials, workflow automation and up to 25 users.

faqs.q: Did QuickBooks Online raise prices in 2026?
faqs.a: Yes. Intuit changed Essentials, Plus and Advanced prices for renewals on or after August 1, 2026; they now list at $85, $140 and $340 a month. Intuit says recent subscribers keep their price for the first six months of their subscription, and Free, Lite and Simple Start prices did not change.

software.name: Xero
software.tagline: Cloud accounting with no per-user license fees and three simple US plans
software.pricing_summary: Three US plans, monthly billing: Early $25/mo, Growing $55/mo, Established $90/mo through September 30, 2026. From October 1, 2026 Xero raises prices for new and existing US subscribers to Early $27, Growing $59 and Established $97, and starts phasing out its multi-organization discount. No per-user license fees on any plan. Early is limited to 20 invoices and 5 bills (auto-reconcile is a $5/mo add-on on Early). Xero Payroll, powered by Gusto, is an optional $36/mo plus $6 per employee or contractor. No free trial is advertised; Xero's offer of 90% off the first 6 months for new US customers ran until September 30, 2026.
software.long_description:
Xero is cloud accounting software headquartered in Wellington, New Zealand, with a US head office in San Mateo, California. Xero says it has been operating since 2006 and serves 5 million customers worldwide. It covers bank reconciliation, invoices and quotes, bills (standard ACH bill payments are included free), expense tracking and reporting, and Xero says more than 1,000 apps connect through the Xero App Store.

The headline point for a growing trades business is that Xero charges no per-user license fees, so adding office staff or your bookkeeper does not raise the subscription. The three US plans are Early, Growing and Established, at $25, $55 and $90 a month through September 30, 2026 and $27, $59 and $97 from October 1, 2026, when Xero raises prices for new and existing US subscribers. Early is limited to 20 invoices and 5 bills; Growing and Established remove those limits, and Established adds project time and cost tracking, employee expenses and multi-currency.

Payroll is an add-on: in the US, Xero Payroll is powered by Gusto and costs $36 a month plus $6 per employee or contractor. Card and ACH payments on invoices run through Stripe, and recurring ACH direct debits through GoCardless. Field-service support varies by tool: Jobber, for example, offers a Xero integration in the US on its Connect and Grow plans that pushes clients, products and services, and invoices one way from Jobber into Xero.

The trade-off: Xero's price does not climb with headcount, but Early is too limited for most working businesses, project tracking needs Established ($90, rising to $97), payroll costs extra, and field-service integrations vary by tool and plan, so check yours before you switch.
software.how_it_works: Connect your bank feeds and Xero brings in transactions for you to reconcile (automatic reconciliation is included from Growing up and is a $5/mo add-on on Early). You send invoices and quotes, capture receipts and bills with Smart Document Capture, pay bills by standard ACH at no charge, and run reports and cash-flow forecasts (30 days on Early, 60 on Growing, 180 on Established). Your accountant and staff work in the same file with no per-user license fees. Payroll runs through the Gusto-powered add-on, invoice payments through Stripe, and field-service tools such as Jobber can push clients and invoices into Xero. Xero's pricing page does not advertise a free trial.

pros_detail.title: No per-user license fees
pros_detail.explanation: Xero lists 'No per-user license fees' on every US plan, so you can give office staff, techs and your accountant their own logins without the bill rising.

pros_detail.title: Simple three-plan lineup
pros_detail.explanation: Three US plans (Early, Growing, Established) are easy to compare; from October 1, 2026 they list at $27, $59 and $97 a month.

pros_detail.title: Free standard ACH bill pay
pros_detail.explanation: Xero says free standard ACH bill payments are included in its business plans; fees apply for other payment methods.

pros_detail.title: Large app marketplace
pros_detail.explanation: Xero says more than 1,000 apps connect through the Xero App Store, and it names Stripe for card and ACH invoice payments, GoCardless for direct debit and Gusto for payroll.

cons_detail.title: Early plan is limited
cons_detail.explanation: Early allows 20 invoices and 5 bills and needs a $5/mo add-on for auto-reconcile, so most working trades businesses need Growing ($55, rising to $59 on October 1, 2026) or above.

cons_detail.title: Price rise on October 1, 2026
cons_detail.explanation: Xero is raising US prices for new and existing subscribers from October 1, 2026 (Early $25 to $27, Growing $55 to $59, Established $90 to $97) and begins phasing out its multi-organization discount the same day.

cons_detail.title: Project tracking only on the top plan
cons_detail.explanation: Tracking time and costs for projects, employee expenses and multi-currency come with Established ($90, rising to $97).

cons_detail.title: Payroll costs extra
cons_detail.explanation: US payroll is the Gusto-powered add-on at $36 a month plus $6 per employee or contractor, on top of the plan.

cons_detail.title: Check your field-service sync
cons_detail.explanation: Integrations vary by tool and plan. Jobber's Xero sync, for example, is one-way and only on its Connect and Grow plans, so confirm what your software supports before switching.

software.best_for: Growing trades businesses that want full cloud accounting with several people in the books and no per-user license fees, and whose field-service tool syncs with Xero
software.weaknesses: Early plan limited to 20 invoices and 5 bills; US prices rise October 1, 2026 ($27/$59/$97); project tracking only on Established; payroll is a paid Gusto-powered add-on; field-service sync varies by tool

ratings.reddit_sentiment: well-liked as the cleaner, unlimited-users alternative to QuickBooks; main hesitation is US integration/accountant familiarity

software.affiliate_payout_note: Xero runs an affiliate/partner program; affiliate_url stays TBD until tracking is confirmed

faqs.q: How much does Xero cost?
faqs.a: Through September 30, 2026: Early $25, Growing $55 and Established $90 a month. From October 1, 2026, for new and existing US subscribers: Early $27, Growing $59 and Established $97. There are no per-user license fees. Early is limited to 20 invoices and 5 bills, so most businesses use Growing or above. Payroll, powered by Gusto, is an add-on at $36 a month plus $6 per employee or contractor.

faqs.q: Is Xero better than QuickBooks for contractors?
faqs.a: It depends on your setup. Xero has three plans and no per-user license fees; QuickBooks Online has six plans, caps users by plan (1 on Simple Start up to 25 on Advanced) and puts job costing on Plus ($140/mo). If your bookkeeper and field-service tool already work in QuickBooks, QBO is simpler; if you need several logins on a budget, Xero is worth pricing out.

faqs.q: Does Xero charge per user?
faqs.a: No. Xero's US pricing page lists 'No per-user license fees' as included on every plan, so adding staff or your accountant does not change the subscription price.

faqs.q: Will my field-service software sync with Xero?
faqs.a: Many tools connect through the Xero App Store, which Xero says lists more than 1,000 apps, but the depth varies. Jobber, for example, offers a Xero integration in the US, Canada, UK, Australia and New Zealand on its Connect and Grow plans; it syncs clients, products and services, and invoices (with payments) one way from Jobber to Xero. Check your own tool before switching.

faqs.q: Does Xero handle payroll?
faqs.a: In the US, Xero Payroll is powered by Gusto and costs $36 a month plus $6 per employee or contractor on top of your Xero plan, so count it in the monthly cost.

software.name: FreshBooks
software.tagline: Invoicing-first accounting for solo and small service businesses
software.pricing_summary: Lite $23/mo (up to 5 billable clients), Plus $43/mo (up to 50 billable clients), Premium $70/mo (unlimited billable clients), Select custom-priced (contact sales; includes 2 team member accounts and Advanced Payments). These are the regular monthly USD rates; FreshBooks advertises an extra 10% off for yearly billing. Additional team members are $11/mo per user on every plan. Promotions change often: on September 30, 2026 FreshBooks offered Lite at $1/mo for the first year or 80% off Plus or Premium for 3 months, with a 30-day money-back guarantee, and a 30-day free trial with no credit card. Add-ons: Advanced Payments $20/mo; Payroll $40/mo plus $6 per employee.
software.long_description:
FreshBooks is cloud accounting built around invoicing and getting paid, aimed at solo operators and small service businesses. It was founded in 2003 by Mike McDerment and is headquartered in Toronto, and FreshBooks says more than 500,000 small businesses have used it. The software covers estimates and proposals, one-off and recurring invoices with automatic reminders and late fees, time and mileage tracking, expenses, client retainers and project profitability, with double-entry accounting reports and accountant access from the Plus plan up.

Pricing is set by how many clients you bill: Lite ($23/mo) covers up to 5 billable clients, Plus ($43/mo) up to 50, and Premium ($70/mo) unlimited, at regular monthly rates; Select is custom-priced. Yearly billing takes an extra 10% off, and FreshBooks runs frequent introductory promotions. Each additional team member is $11/mo.

Clients can pay invoices by card (2.9% + $0.30), ACH bank transfer (1%), Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal or Affirm buy-now-pay-later, and you can request deposits on estimates; FreshBooks Payments is powered by Stripe. FreshBooks Payroll, run with Gusto, costs $40/mo plus $6 per employee.

The trade-off: FreshBooks keeps quoting, billing and getting paid simple, but the client caps on Lite and Plus, the $11/mo per extra team member, and the lack of accountant access and double-entry reports on Lite add up for a growing shop. Its plan comparison does not list inventory tracking, so contractors who stock materials, or whose field-service tool syncs only with QuickBooks Online or Xero, should compare those first.
software.how_it_works: FreshBooks centers on the quote-to-paid workflow: you send estimates and proposals (with deposits if you want them), turn them into branded one-off or recurring invoices, track time, mileage and expenses against clients and projects, and collect card, ACH, digital-wallet, PayPal or Affirm payments against those invoices, with automatic reminders and late fees. Reports cover the bookkeeping side, with double-entry accounting reports and accountant access on Plus and up. You pick a plan by the number of clients you bill (Lite up to 5, Plus up to 50, Premium unlimited) and add team members at $11/mo each. A 30-day free trial needs no credit card.

pros_detail.title: Built around invoicing
pros_detail.explanation: Estimates, proposals, one-off and recurring invoices, automatic reminders and online payment are the core of the product, which matches what a solo trades operator does most.

pros_detail.title: Many ways for clients to pay
pros_detail.explanation: Cards (2.9% + $0.30), ACH bank transfer (1%), Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal and Affirm buy-now-pay-later, with FreshBooks Payments powered by Stripe and deposits available on estimates.

pros_detail.title: Time, mileage and project tracking
pros_detail.explanation: Unlimited time tracking, mobile mileage tracking, client retainers and project profitability are built in, so a small crew can quote, track and bill in one tool.

pros_detail.title: Low entry price and free trial
pros_detail.explanation: Lite lists at $23/mo (less with yearly billing or a promotion), and a 30-day free trial needs no credit card.

cons_detail.title: Client limits on lower tiers
cons_detail.explanation: Lite caps you at 5 billable clients and Plus at 50, so a trades shop with many one-off customers can be pushed to Premium ($70/mo) quickly.

cons_detail.title: Per-user fees for the team
cons_detail.explanation: Each additional team member costs $11/mo on every plan (Select includes 2), while Xero charges no per-user license fees.

cons_detail.title: Lite lacks accountant access
cons_detail.explanation: Double-entry accounting reports and accountant access start at Plus ($43/mo), so the cheapest plan is not set up for handing your books to a bookkeeper.

cons_detail.title: No inventory in the plan list
cons_detail.explanation: FreshBooks' plan comparison does not list inventory tracking; contractors who stock materials may need QuickBooks Online Plus or another tool.

cons_detail.title: Check your field-service sync
cons_detail.explanation: Before committing, confirm that your field-service tool offers a FreshBooks sync; Jobber, for example, documents QuickBooks Online and Xero integrations.

software.best_for: Solo and small service contractors (handymen, cleaners, painters, small crews) who bill a limited number of clients and want simple quoting, invoicing and online payment
software.weaknesses: Billable-client caps on Lite (5) and Plus (50); $11/mo per extra team member; no accountant access or double-entry reports on Lite; inventory not in the plan list; confirm your field-service tool syncs with FreshBooks

ratings.reddit_sentiment: loved by solo and small service businesses for invoicing ease; seen as light on deep accounting for larger shops

software.affiliate_payout_note: FreshBooks runs an established affiliate program; affiliate_url stays TBD until tracking is confirmed

faqs.q: How much does FreshBooks cost?
faqs.a: Lite is $23/mo (up to 5 billable clients), Plus $43/mo (up to 50), Premium $70/mo (unlimited) and Select is custom-priced. Those are the regular monthly rates; yearly billing takes an extra 10% off, and FreshBooks often runs introductory promotions. Additional team members cost $11/mo each, Advanced Payments is $20/mo and Payroll is $40/mo plus $6 per employee.

faqs.q: Is FreshBooks real accounting or just invoicing?
faqs.a: It is accounting built around invoicing. FreshBooks handles estimates, invoices, payments, time, mileage and expenses, and its Plus, Premium and Select plans add double-entry accounting reports and accountant access. Its plan comparison does not list inventory tracking, so shops that stock materials may prefer QuickBooks Online or Xero.

faqs.q: Who should use FreshBooks instead of QuickBooks?
faqs.a: Solo operators and small service businesses (handymen, cleaners, painters, small crews) who bill a limited number of clients and want simple quoting, invoicing and online payment. If you need inventory, job costing across many projects, many users, or your field-service tool syncs only with QuickBooks, QuickBooks Online is the more natural fit.

faqs.q: What are FreshBooks' client limits?
faqs.a: Lite supports up to 5 billable clients and Plus up to 50; Premium and Select are unlimited. If you bill more clients than your plan allows, you need to move up a plan, which matters for trades businesses with many one-off customers.

faqs.q: Does FreshBooks integrate with my field-service software?
faqs.a: It depends on the tool. FreshBooks connects to apps through its App Store and runs payments through Stripe and payroll with Gusto, but field-service syncs vary. Jobber, for example, documents QuickBooks Online and Xero integrations, so confirm your own software supports FreshBooks before committing.

software.name: Wave
software.tagline: Free accounting and invoicing for very small and new businesses
software.pricing_summary: Starter plan free ($0/mo): unlimited estimates, invoices, bills and bookkeeping records. Pro $19 USD/mo or $190 USD/yr: adds automatic bank-transaction import and categorizing, unlimited receipt capture, late-payment reminders and extra users. Card processing 2.9% + $0.60 (Amex 3.4% + $0.60); bank (ACH) payments 1% with a $1 minimum; Pro waives the $0.60 on the first 10 card transactions each month. Payroll add-on (US) $40/mo base + $6 per active employee and $6 per contractor paid. Receipts add-on for Starter $8 USD/mo or $72/yr (included in Pro); Wave Advisors bookkeeping from $149 USD/mo.
software.long_description:
Wave is small-business accounting software with a free Starter plan, made by Wave Financial of Toronto, which H&R Block acquired in 2019. Wave says it has helped more than 5.9 million small business owners in the US and Canada since 2010. The free plan covers unlimited estimates, invoices, bills and bookkeeping records in what Wave calls real double-entry accounting, with profit and loss, balance sheet and cash-flow reports.

For a brand-new or very small trades operator, Wave removes the subscription as a barrier to getting organized. The Pro plan ($19/mo or $190/yr) adds automatic import, merging and categorizing of bank transactions, unlimited receipt capture, automatic late-payment reminders, branded invoices and extra users. Wave earns the rest from add-ons: card and bank payments on invoices, Wave Payroll ($40/mo plus $6 per active employee and $6 per contractor paid in the US), a Receipts add-on for Starter users ($8/mo) and Wave Advisors bookkeeping from $149/mo.

Card payments cost 2.9% + $0.60 per transaction (3.4% + $0.60 for Amex) and bank (ACH) payments 1% with a $1 minimum; Pro waives the $0.60 on the first 10 card transactions each month. Wave's payments page says it runs periodic credit risk assessments and may hold funds while it asks for more information, and its BBB profile lists 235 complaints closed in the last three years, so read the payout terms before relying on Wave Payments for cash flow.

The trade-off: Wave lets you keep real books and send unlimited invoices for $0, but bank automation and extra users need Pro, card payments carry a $0.60 fixed fee (FreshBooks charges $0.30), and you should confirm your field-service tool syncs with Wave before relying on it.
software.how_it_works: Sign up for the free Starter plan and you can send unlimited estimates and invoices, record bills and expenses, and keep double-entry books, entering bank transactions yourself. Pro ($19/mo) connects your bank and card accounts through Plaid to import, merge and categorize transactions automatically, adds unlimited receipt capture and late-payment reminders, and lets you add users as admin, editor or viewer. On either plan you can accept card and bank payments on invoices (Wave says payouts take 1-2 business days for cards and 1-7 for bank payments) and add Wave Payroll. There is no trial because Starter is free.

pros_detail.title: Free core accounting
pros_detail.explanation: The Starter plan is $0 and includes unlimited estimates, invoices, bills and bookkeeping records, removing software cost as a barrier for brand-new or very small trades businesses.

pros_detail.title: Real double-entry books
pros_detail.explanation: Wave describes itself as real double-entry accounting software, with profit and loss, balance sheet and cash-flow reports your accountant can work from.

pros_detail.title: Low-cost upgrade
pros_detail.explanation: Pro is $19/mo or $190/yr and adds automatic bank imports, unlimited receipt capture, late-payment reminders and extra users.

pros_detail.title: Pay only for add-ons you use
pros_detail.explanation: Payments, payroll ($40/mo plus $6 per active employee and $6 per contractor paid) and bookkeeping help (from $149/mo) are optional, so a lean operation pays only when it needs them.

pros_detail.title: Bank-payment option
pros_detail.explanation: Customers can pay invoices by bank transfer at 1% with a $1 minimum, cheaper than card processing on larger jobs.

cons_detail.title: Bank automation needs Pro
cons_detail.explanation: On the free Starter plan you enter bank transactions yourself; automatic import, merging and categorizing through Plaid require Pro ($19/mo).

cons_detail.title: Higher fixed card fee
cons_detail.explanation: Card payments cost 2.9% + $0.60 (Amex 3.4% + $0.60); Pro waives the $0.60 only on the first 10 card transactions a month. FreshBooks charges 2.9% + $0.30.

cons_detail.title: Payment holds possible
cons_detail.explanation: Wave's payments page says it runs periodic credit risk assessments and may hold funds and ask for more information, which can delay cash for a small business.

cons_detail.title: Check your field-service sync
cons_detail.explanation: Before relying on Wave, confirm your field-service tool syncs with it; Jobber, for example, documents QuickBooks Online and Xero integrations.

cons_detail.title: Extra users need Pro
cons_detail.explanation: Adding admins, editors or viewers requires Pro; Starter only lets you add a payroll manager or a Block Advisors tax pro.

software.best_for: Brand-new, solo or very small trades businesses that want free double-entry books and unlimited invoicing while watching every dollar
software.weaknesses: Bank automation and extra users need Pro ($19/mo); card fee of 2.9% + $0.60; Wave may hold payment funds during risk reviews; confirm your field-service tool syncs with Wave
software.reputation_flag: Wave Financial's BBB profile lists 235 complaints closed in the last three years as of 30 September 2026. Wave is BBB-accredited (since 2013) with an A- rating. Wave's own payments page says it runs periodic credit risk assessments and may hold funds and request more information, so confirm payout and hold terms before relying on Wave Payments for cash flow.

ratings.reddit_sentiment: the go-to free option for tiny businesses; complaints about support and features moving from free to paid

software.affiliate_payout_note: No confirmed standard affiliate program (Wave is owned by H&R Block); affiliate_url stays TBD

faqs.q: Is Wave accounting still free in 2026?
faqs.a: Yes. The Starter plan is $0 and includes unlimited estimates, invoices, bills and bookkeeping records. Automatic bank imports, unlimited receipt capture, late-payment reminders and extra users need Pro ($19/mo or $190/yr), and payments and payroll cost extra.

faqs.q: Who should use Wave?
faqs.a: Brand-new, solo or very small trades businesses watching every dollar that want real books and unlimited invoicing for free. If you need job costing, inventory, several users or a field-service sync, check whether Wave covers it or compare QuickBooks Online, Xero or FreshBooks.

faqs.q: What does Wave charge for?
faqs.a: Pro is $19/mo ($190/yr). Card payments cost 2.9% + $0.60 (Amex 3.4% + $0.60), with Pro waiving the $0.60 on the first 10 card transactions a month; bank payments cost 1% with a $1 minimum. Wave Payroll is $40/mo plus $6 per active employee and $6 per contractor paid in the US. The Receipts add-on is $8/mo for Starter users, and Wave Advisors bookkeeping starts at $149/mo.

faqs.q: What are the downsides of Wave?
faqs.a: Bank automation and extra users need Pro; card processing carries a $0.60 fixed fee (FreshBooks charges $0.30); Wave says it may hold payment funds during credit risk reviews; and you need to confirm your field-service tool syncs with Wave.

faqs.q: Will my field-service software sync with Wave?
faqs.a: Check before you commit. Jobber, for example, documents integrations with QuickBooks Online and Xero. If your field-service tool has no Wave sync, you would re-enter invoices and payments in Wave by hand.

software.name: QuickBooks Desktop / Enterprise
software.tagline: QuickBooks' Windows desktop accounting for larger contractors, with a Construction & Contractors edition
software.pricing_summary: Starting at $2,210/yr for Gold (about $184/mo) and $2,717/yr for Platinum, both annual subscriptions for 1-10 or up to 30 users, and $5,363/yr for Diamond (monthly subscription only, up to 40 users), per Intuit's pricing page; exact pricing comes from its custom pricing tool or Intuit sales (800-450-8469). Gold includes QuickBooks Desktop Enhanced Payroll (plus up to $3 per employee a month), Advanced Reporting and multi-company management; Platinum adds Advanced Inventory, Advanced Pricing, intercompany transactions and bill and PO approval workflows; Diamond adds Assisted Payroll ($2.50 per employee per pay period) and QuickBooks Time Elite (billed per employee). Cloud hosting costs extra. A 30-day free trial needs no credit card, and annual plans carry a 60-day money-back guarantee.
software.long_description:
QuickBooks Desktop Enterprise is Intuit's Windows-installed accounting software for larger small businesses, sold in industry editions that include Construction & Contractors. Intuit says the contractor edition tracks job costs in real time, takes advance prepayments on estimates and sales orders, and comes with a contractor chart of accounts and customizable contractor reports, and that Enterprise's job cost tracking covers labor, materials, deadlines and change orders. Billing rate levels, available in the Contractor, Professional Services and Accountant editions, fill in the right labor rate on an invoice based on who did the work.

Product direction matters here. Intuit stopped selling new QuickBooks Desktop Pro Plus, Premier Plus and Mac Plus subscriptions, and Desktop Enhanced Payroll, to US customers after September 30, 2024. Existing subscribers can keep renewing, and Intuit says Enterprise is not affected: new and existing customers can still buy or renew it.

Enterprise runs on Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit), on your own machines or on Intuit's cloud hosting for an extra fee, with up to 30 users on Gold and Platinum and up to 40 on Diamond; there is no Mac version. For field work, Diamond includes QuickBooks Time Elite for mobile time tracking, and contractors can connect a field-service or construction tool; Knowify, for example, syncs both ways with QuickBooks Desktop on its Enterprise plan.

The trade-off: Enterprise brings a contractor edition, billing rate levels, payroll built into the plan and room for up to 40 users, but it is Windows-only and starts at $2,210 a year, with the exact price set by a custom quote. Small crews can compare QuickBooks Online, which offers project profitability tracking from its Plus plan.
software.how_it_works: Enterprise installs on Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) PCs, with a Windows Server option for multi-user setups, or runs on Intuit's cloud hosting for an extra fee. Users share one company file (up to 30 on Gold and Platinum, up to 40 on Diamond). In the contractor edition you assign costs to jobs, take prepayments on estimates and sales orders, set billing rate levels by worker, and run contractor and job reports, with Advanced Reporting on every plan. Payroll is part of the plan (Enhanced Payroll on Gold and Platinum, Assisted Payroll on Diamond). You get a custom quote online or from Intuit sales (800-450-8469); a 30-day free trial needs no credit card, and annual plans have a 60-day money-back guarantee.

pros_detail.title: Contractor edition with job costing
pros_detail.explanation: Intuit's Construction & Contractors edition tracks job costs in real time, takes prepayments on estimates and sales orders, and includes a contractor chart of accounts and contractor reports.

pros_detail.title: Billing rate levels
pros_detail.explanation: Set different service rates by employee or vendor; QuickBooks fills in the right rate on invoices with billable time based on who did the work (Contractor, Professional Services and Accountant editions).

pros_detail.title: Room for up to 40 users
pros_detail.explanation: Gold and Platinum allow up to 30 users and Diamond up to 40, and Platinum adds Advanced Inventory, Advanced Pricing and bill and PO approval workflows for shops carrying materials.

pros_detail.title: Payroll included in the plan
pros_detail.explanation: Gold and Platinum include Enhanced Payroll (plus up to $3 per employee a month) and Diamond includes Assisted Payroll ($2.50 per employee per pay period), so payroll is not a separate subscription.

pros_detail.title: Try before you buy
pros_detail.explanation: A 30-day free trial needs no credit card, and annual plans carry a 60-day money-back guarantee.

cons_detail.title: Desktop line is shrinking
cons_detail.explanation: Intuit stopped selling new Desktop Pro Plus, Premier Plus and Mac Plus subscriptions to US customers after September 30, 2024. Enterprise is not affected, but weigh the long-term direction of desktop software.

cons_detail.title: Annual cost runs into the thousands
cons_detail.explanation: Intuit lists starting prices of $2,210/yr for Gold, $2,717/yr for Platinum and $5,363/yr for Diamond, which is sold only as a monthly subscription; your exact price comes from its custom pricing tool or sales.

cons_detail.title: Windows only
cons_detail.explanation: Enterprise needs Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) and has no Mac version; working remotely means Intuit's cloud hosting at extra cost.

cons_detail.title: Field work needs add-ons
cons_detail.explanation: Mobile time tracking comes through QuickBooks Time Elite (included with Diamond), and scheduling and dispatch need a separate field-service tool connected to QuickBooks.

cons_detail.title: More than small shops need
cons_detail.explanation: For a solo or one- to three-person operation, a desktop system sized for up to 40 users and starting at $2,210 a year is a lot to take on; QuickBooks Online is simpler to start with.

software.best_for: Established contractors and specialty trades running many jobs at once who want Windows desktop accounting with a contractor edition, billing rate levels and room for up to 40 users
software.weaknesses: Intuit stopped selling new Desktop Pro Plus, Premier Plus and Mac Plus in the US (Enterprise still sold); starting prices of $2,210-$5,363 a year; Windows-only; field work needs QuickBooks Time or a separate field-service tool; a lot for small shops

ratings.reddit_sentiment: regarded as the deepest job costing in the QuickBooks line and the place established contractors graduate to, but criticized as Desktop-only, pricey, and subject to rising annual fees

software.affiliate_program: QuickBooks affiliate program exists (skews to QBO); new Enterprise deals typically flow through the QuickBooks Solution Provider reseller channel, not self-serve affiliate links
software.affiliate_payout_note: affiliate_url stays TBD; Enterprise is reseller-channel (QSP), not a simple affiliate link

faqs.q: Is QuickBooks Desktop being discontinued?
faqs.a: Not entirely. Intuit stopped selling new QuickBooks Desktop Pro Plus, Premier Plus, Mac Plus and Desktop Enhanced Payroll subscriptions to US customers after September 30, 2024. Existing subscribers can keep renewing, and Intuit says Enterprise is not affected: new and existing customers can still buy or renew it.

faqs.q: Why do contractors use QuickBooks Enterprise over QuickBooks Online?
faqs.a: Mainly for the Construction & Contractors edition: real-time job costing, prepayments on estimates and sales orders, billing rate levels by worker, a contractor chart of accounts and contractor reports, plus room for up to 40 users and Advanced Inventory on Platinum. Smaller shops can compare QuickBooks Online, which offers project profitability tracking from its Plus plan.

faqs.q: How much does QuickBooks Enterprise cost in 2026?
faqs.a: Intuit's pricing page lists starting prices of $2,210 a year for Gold and $2,717 a year for Platinum (annual subscriptions) and $5,363 a year for Diamond (monthly subscription only), with exact pricing from its custom pricing tool or Intuit sales at 800-450-8469. The per-employee payroll costs are listed: Enhanced Payroll up to $3 per employee a month on Gold and Platinum, and Assisted Payroll $2.50 per employee per pay period on Diamond. Annual plans have a 60-day money-back guarantee.

faqs.q: Does QuickBooks Enterprise have a field/mobile app for techs?
faqs.a: Enterprise itself is Windows software. Diamond includes QuickBooks Time Elite for mobile time tracking that syncs with QuickBooks, and Intuit's contractor page points to field-service management integrations for crews in the field. Knowify, a construction tool, syncs both ways with QuickBooks Desktop on its Enterprise plan.

software.name: Sage (Sage 50 + Sage Accounting)
software.tagline: Sage 50: installed accounting software with job, phase and cost code tracking, inventory and purchase orders
software.pricing_summary: Sage 50 has three US plans with a minimum one-year commitment: Pro Accounting from $128.67/mo (one user), Premium Accounting from $182.50/mo (1-5 users) and Quantum Accounting from $271.17/mo (1-40 users), with prices rising by number of users. Sage's cloud product, Sage Accounting, is not sold in the US.
software.long_description:
Sage 50 Accounting is the US edition of Sage's small-business accounting software. It is published by Sage Software, Inc., part of The Sage Group plc, a UK public company registered in Newcastle upon Tyne, England. The US product grew out of Peachtree Accounting, which Sage bought in 1998 and rebranded under the Sage 50 name in 2013. Sage's lighter cloud product, Sage Accounting, is not sold in the US (its help site lists only the UK, Ireland and Canada), so for US contractors this entry covers Sage 50.

For trades, the draw is job costing. Every plan tracks jobs by job ID, with costs and revenue recorded against each job. Premium Accounting and higher add phases and cost codes, so a job can be split into stages with labor, materials and other cost types tracked inside each, plus job estimates of revenue and expenses, change orders, and time and billing for invoicing customers by job, phase or cost code. Sage's help site says job reports show whether a job is over or under budget for each phase.

Sage 50 also handles inventory (including assemblies built from components, and serialized inventory in Premium and higher), purchase orders and bank connections, and it runs payroll if your Sage service plan includes payroll. The 2026 release added AR Automation, which shares invoices with customers, sends payment reminders and collects payments; it needs an active cloud subscription.

The trade-off: Sage 50 costs more than simple cloud bookkeeping (Pro starts at $128.67/mo on a one-year commitment), phases and cost codes need Premium or higher, and it is installed accounting software with no scheduling or dispatch, so field crews still need a separate field-service app.
software.how_it_works: You install Sage 50 and set up your company, customers, vendors and inventory items. Jobs can be set up as a job ID alone or, in Premium Accounting and higher, with phases and cost codes; you enter estimated revenue and expenses for each job and assign costs to jobs as you record purchases, time and payroll. Premium and higher can bill customers from time and expense tickets by job, phase or cost code. Sage 50 connects to banks for transactions, can send email through Microsoft 365 Outlook, and runs payroll if your service plan includes it. Plans are subscriptions with a minimum one-year commitment, and some features, such as AR Automation, need an active cloud subscription.

pros_detail.title: Job costing with phases and cost codes
pros_detail.explanation: Premium Accounting and higher split jobs into phases and cost codes, with estimated revenue and expenses per job and job reports that show over- or under-budget phases.

pros_detail.title: Inventory and purchase orders
pros_detail.explanation: Tracks stocked items, assemblies built from components and purchase orders; Premium and higher add serialized inventory.

pros_detail.title: Time and billing by job
pros_detail.explanation: Premium and higher can invoice customers for billable time and expenses by job, phase or cost code.

pros_detail.title: Room to grow
pros_detail.explanation: Sage says Quantum Accounting scales to 40 users, with role-based user permissions.

cons_detail.title: Higher price and a one-year commitment
cons_detail.explanation: Plans start at $128.67/mo with a minimum one-year commitment, and the price rises with plan and user count.

cons_detail.title: Phases and cost codes need Premium
cons_detail.explanation: Pro Accounting tracks jobs by job ID only; phases, cost codes, change orders and time and billing start at Premium Accounting.

cons_detail.title: Installed software
cons_detail.explanation: Sage 50 is software you install, and newer features such as AR Automation need an active cloud subscription.

cons_detail.title: No scheduling or dispatch
cons_detail.explanation: It is accounting software; pair it with a field-service app for scheduling and dispatch.

software.best_for: Established US contractors who want job costing by phase and cost code, inventory and purchase orders in one accounting package
software.weaknesses: Costs more than simple cloud bookkeeping, with a minimum one-year commitment; phases and cost codes need Premium or higher; installed software; no scheduling or dispatch

ratings.reddit_sentiment: respected for real job costing and inventory in Sage 50, but buyers gripe about price increases and support

software.affiliate_program: Yes: Sage Affiliate Program (via Impact.com) plus the Sage Partner Network
software.affiliate_payout_note: affiliate_url stays TBD until the Impact.com tracking link is confirmed

faqs.q: Does Sage 50 do job costing for contractors?
faqs.a: Yes. Every Sage 50 plan tracks jobs by job ID. Sage's help site says phases and cost codes are available in Premium Accounting and higher, along with job estimates of revenue and expenses, change orders, and time and billing by job, phase or cost code.

faqs.q: Does Sage sell a low-cost cloud plan in the US?
faqs.a: No. Sage's cloud product, Sage Accounting, is not sold in the US; its help site lists only the UK, Ireland and Canada. In the US, Sage sells Sage 50. A solo who only needs invoicing, expenses and bank reconciliation can compare the lower-priced tools in this category.

faqs.q: How much does Sage 50 cost?
faqs.a: Sage's US pricing page on 2026-09-30 showed Pro Accounting from $128.67/mo, Premium Accounting from $182.50/mo and Quantum Accounting from $271.17/mo, with a minimum one-year commitment and prices that rise with the number of users.

faqs.q: Who owns Sage 50?
faqs.a: Sage 50 in the US is published by Sage Software, Inc., part of The Sage Group plc, a UK public company registered in Newcastle upon Tyne. The US product grew out of Peachtree Accounting, which Sage bought in 1998 and rebranded as Sage 50 in 2013.

software.name: Zoho Books
software.tagline: Low-cost online accounting with a free plan for small revenue and job profitability from the Professional plan
software.pricing_summary: Free $0 (while revenue for the financial year stays under $50K; 1 user plus 1 accountant; up to 1,000 invoices a year) · Standard $15/mo · Professional $40/mo · Premium $60/mo · Elite $120/mo · Ultimate $240/mo, billed annually ($20, $50, $70, $150 and $275 billed monthly). Paid plans include 3, 5, 10, 10 and 15 users; extra users $2.50/mo billed annually or $3/mo monthly. 14-day free trial.
software.headquartered: Chennai, India (US offices in Pleasanton, CA and Austin, TX)
software.long_description:
Zoho Books is online accounting software from Zoho Corporation, which started as AdventNet in New Jersey in 1996, renamed itself Zoho in 2009 and launched Zoho Books in 2011. Zoho has its Estancia campus in Chennai, India, and US offices in Pleasanton, California and Austin, Texas, and says it has never taken money from investors.

The Free plan stays available as long as revenue for the financial year is under $50,000. It covers one user plus an accountant and up to 1,000 invoices a year, with quotes, expenses, mileage tracking, bank reconciliation, a customer portal, online payments, and 1099 and W-9 management. Standard ($15/mo billed annually, 3 users) adds sales tax and use tax tracking. For trades that want per-job numbers, the plan to look at is Professional ($40/mo billed annually, 5 users): it adds projects, billable timesheets, project profitability, inventory tracking, and sales and purchase orders.

Zoho sells related apps that connect to Books. Zoho Payroll, which Zoho says handles federal, state and local tax payments in all 50 states, posts payroll journal entries into Books. Zoho FSM, Zoho's field-service app, has a two-way sync with Books for companies, contacts, and services and parts, and turns work orders into invoices. Books also has mobile apps and connects to Tax1099 and Yearli for 1099 filing.

The trade-off: the Free and Standard plans are cheap, but projects, timesheets and inventory start at Professional, advanced inventory and warehouses start at Elite ($120/mo billed annually), scheduling and dispatch need Zoho FSM as a separate app, and Books is general small-business accounting rather than construction accounting.
software.how_it_works: Start on the Free plan or a 14-day trial of a paid plan, connect your bank accounts, and send invoices and quotes that customers can pay online through a payment link or the customer portal, with automatic payment reminders. On Professional and higher, you set up projects, staff log time with a timer on the web, mobile app or browser extension, and you bill timesheets and see each project's profitability. A vendor portal lets suppliers receive purchase orders and track bill payments. Zoho Payroll posts payroll journal entries into Books, and Zoho FSM syncs customers and services with Books and turns field work orders into invoices.

pros_detail.title: Free plan for small revenue
pros_detail.explanation: Free while revenue for the financial year stays under $50,000, with invoices, quotes, expenses, mileage and bank reconciliation for one user plus an accountant.

pros_detail.title: Low paid entry price
pros_detail.explanation: Standard is $15/mo billed annually ($20 monthly) with 3 users and sales tax tracking.

pros_detail.title: Job profitability on Professional
pros_detail.explanation: Professional ($40/mo billed annually) adds projects, billable timesheets, project profitability, inventory tracking and purchase orders.

pros_detail.title: Online payments and customer portal
pros_detail.explanation: Customers can pay invoices online through a payment link or the portal, with automatic reminders.

pros_detail.title: Zoho's own payroll and field-service apps
pros_detail.explanation: Zoho Payroll posts journal entries into Books, and Zoho FSM syncs customers and services with Books and turns work orders into invoices.

cons_detail.title: Job tracking needs Professional
cons_detail.explanation: Projects, timesheets and project profitability are not in Free or Standard; they start at $40/mo billed annually.

cons_detail.title: Field service is a separate app
cons_detail.explanation: Scheduling and dispatch live in Zoho FSM, a separate product, not inside Books.

cons_detail.title: Advanced inventory costs more
cons_detail.explanation: Advanced inventory control and warehouses start at Elite, $120/mo billed annually.

cons_detail.title: Monthly billing costs more
cons_detail.explanation: Paying month to month costs $5-$35 more per month than annual billing, depending on the plan.

cons_detail.title: Not construction accounting
cons_detail.explanation: It is general small-business accounting; Zoho's plan list does not include construction billing features such as AIA progress billing or retainage.

software.best_for: Cost-conscious solo and small trades (plumbers, electricians, HVAC, handymen, small GCs) that want low-cost full accounting, with per-job profitability from the Professional plan, especially if they use other Zoho apps
software.weaknesses: Projects, timesheets and inventory start at Professional ($40/mo billed annually); field service needs the separate Zoho FSM app; advanced inventory starts at Elite; monthly billing costs more than annual; not construction accounting

ratings.reddit_sentiment: widely praised as the best-value full accounting, especially inside the Zoho suite; the recurring knock is support responsiveness

software.affiliate_program: Yes, Zoho Affiliate Program: 15% commission for the first 12 months (up to ~18-20% at higher tiers), 90-day cookie
software.affiliate_payout_note: affiliate_url stays TBD until the Zoho affiliate tracking link is confirmed

faqs.q: Is Zoho Books really free for a small contractor?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as revenue for the financial year stays under $50,000. The Free plan covers one user plus an accountant and up to 1,000 invoices a year, with quotes, expenses, mileage tracking, bank reconciliation and online payments. Above that, Standard is $15/mo billed annually ($20 monthly).

faqs.q: Does Zoho Books do job costing?
faqs.a: Partly. From the Professional plan ($40/mo billed annually), Zoho Books has projects, billable timesheets and project profitability, so you can see time and costs per job. Zoho's plan list does not include construction billing features such as AIA progress billing or retainage, so complex GC accounting needs a construction-focused tool.

faqs.q: Can Zoho Books handle my payroll?
faqs.a: Zoho sells payroll as a separate app, Zoho Payroll. Zoho says it handles federal, state and local tax payments for all 50 states and posts payroll journal entries into Zoho Books. Check Zoho Payroll's own pricing before you sign up.

faqs.q: Does Zoho Books work for field-service scheduling?
faqs.a: Not by itself. Scheduling and dispatch live in Zoho FSM, a separate app. Zoho says FSM has a two-way sync with Zoho Books for companies, contacts, and services and parts, and converts work orders into invoices.

software.name: Patriot Accounting
software.tagline: Low-cost online bookkeeping from Canton, Ohio that posts Patriot Payroll entries to your books automatically
software.pricing_summary: Accounting Basic $20/mo · Accounting Premium $30/mo. 30-day free trial, then 50% off for the first 3 months. Unlimited users at no extra charge. Online invoice payments run through Stripe: 2.9% + $0.30 per card payment; 0.8% per ACH payment, capped at $5.
software.long_description:
Patriot Accounting is online bookkeeping software from Patriot Software LLC of Canton, Ohio, which also sells Patriot Payroll. The Better Business Bureau lists the company as started in August 2002, with Kyle Dreger as CEO.

Patriot lists two plans: Accounting Basic at $20/mo and Accounting Premium at $30/mo, with a 30-day free trial followed by 50% off for three months. Both include unlimited customers, invoices and vendors, unlimited users at no extra charge, bank connections through Plaid (or spreadsheet upload), invoicing with online card and ACH payments through Stripe, departments for grouping transactions in reports, and what Patriot calls patented dual-ledger accounting, which tracks cash, modified cash and accrual books at the same time. Premium adds estimates, recurring invoices, invoice payment reminders, receipt and document management, subaccounts and accounting user permissions.

The main pairing is Patriot Payroll: if you use both, Patriot creates a journal entry in your books automatically each time you run payroll. Online payments carry Stripe's fees, which Patriot lists as 2.9% plus $0.30 per card payment with no cap and 0.8% per ACH payment capped at $5 (plus $1.50 when a customer uses instant bank verification); the first payout has a waiting period of 7 to 14 days.

The trade-off: Patriot is simple, low-cost bookkeeping, but its help center describes no job costing (departments are the closest tool), estimates and recurring invoices need Premium, and moving in from QuickBooks means entering or importing your trial balance and uploading customer and vendor lists rather than using a direct import tool.
software.how_it_works: Start the 30-day free trial and work through the setup checklist on the Accounting home page: upload your chart of accounts, connect your bank through Plaid or upload a spreadsheet, and enter or import your opening trial balance. Customer and vendor lists import from .xls, .xlsx or .csv files; open invoices and bills are entered one at a time. You then send invoices that customers can pay online by card or ACH through Stripe, and you can tag transactions with departments to filter reports. If you also use Patriot Payroll, each payroll run posts a journal entry to your books automatically.

pros_detail.title: Low monthly price
pros_detail.explanation: Accounting Basic is $20/mo and Premium $30/mo, with a 30-day free trial and then 50% off for three months.

pros_detail.title: Unlimited users at no charge
pros_detail.explanation: Patriot says you can add users without extra charges on both plans, along with unlimited customers, invoices and vendors.

pros_detail.title: Automatic payroll entries
pros_detail.explanation: With Patriot Payroll, each payroll run creates a journal entry in Patriot Accounting automatically.

pros_detail.title: Online invoice payments
pros_detail.explanation: Customers can pay invoices by card or ACH through Stripe on both plans.

pros_detail.title: Dual-ledger accounting
pros_detail.explanation: Patriot tracks cash, modified cash and accrual bases at the same time, so you can view reports either way without converting.

cons_detail.title: No job costing
cons_detail.explanation: Patriot's help center describes departments for grouping transactions but no job costing, a gap for shops that track profit by job.

cons_detail.title: Key invoicing tools need Premium
cons_detail.explanation: Estimates, recurring invoices, payment reminders and receipt management are Premium-only.

cons_detail.title: No QuickBooks import tool
cons_detail.explanation: Moving from QuickBooks means entering or importing your trial balance and uploading customer and vendor spreadsheets; open invoices and bills are entered one at a time.

cons_detail.title: Stripe fees and first-payout wait
cons_detail.explanation: Card payments cost 2.9% plus $0.30 with no cap, and the first Stripe payout waits 7 to 14 days.

software.best_for: Cost-conscious solo and small US trades (plumber, electrician, small HVAC, handyman) that want simple books, ideally alongside Patriot Payroll
software.weaknesses: No job costing; estimates, recurring invoices and payment reminders need Premium; no direct QuickBooks import tool; Stripe card fees and a 7-14 day wait on the first payout

ratings.reddit_sentiment: consistently praised as cheap, simple, and well-supported for solo/micro businesses; the known limit is weak job costing

software.affiliate_program: Yes: Patriot Affiliate Program (~$150 per new paying customer) plus an Accountant Partner Program
software.affiliate_payout_note: affiliate_url stays TBD until the Patriot affiliate tracking link is confirmed

faqs.q: How much does Patriot Accounting cost?
faqs.a: Patriot lists Accounting Basic at $20/mo and Accounting Premium at $30/mo. There is a 30-day free trial, then 50% off for the first three months. Online invoice payments through Stripe carry Stripe's fees: 2.9% plus $0.30 per card payment and 0.8% per ACH payment, capped at $5.

faqs.q: Is Patriot good for contractors with job costing needs?
faqs.a: Not really. Patriot's help center describes departments, which let you tag invoices, bills and other transactions and filter reports by group, but it does not describe job costing. If per-job profitability is central to your business, look at the tools in this category that offer job costing.

faqs.q: Does Patriot Accounting work with Patriot Payroll?
faqs.a: Yes. If you use both Patriot Payroll and Patriot Accounting, Patriot creates a journal entry in your books automatically each time you run payroll.

faqs.q: Can Patriot sync with QuickBooks?
faqs.a: No. Patriot Accounting is meant to replace QuickBooks as your books, and its help center describes no QuickBooks sync or import tool: you enter or import your trial balance and upload customer and vendor spreadsheets. Patriot Payroll, a separate product, can send payroll journal entries to QuickBooks Online.

software.name: Striven
software.tagline: All-in-one business platform with built-in accounting, job costing and technician scheduling, priced per user
software.pricing_summary: Standard $35/user/mo · Enterprise $70/user/mo, on monthly plans; teams under 5 users add $25/user. Customer, vendor and career portals are free up to 100 customers, vendors or applications a month, $99/mo up to 500, and $499/mo unlimited. Free trial offered (length not stated on the pricing page).
software.headquartered: United States (operated by Miles IT, Inc.)
software.long_description:
Striven is an all-in-one business platform made by Miles IT, Inc., a technology company that says it has operated under the same ownership since 1997 and is wholly owned by its founder and CEO, Chris Miles, and family trusts. Striven combines accounting, CRM and sales, project and task management, inventory, HR, portals, workflows and field service in one system, and has industry pages for HVAC, plumbing, electrical contracting, landscaping, construction and other field services.

Accounting is built in rather than synced: Striven lists a general ledger, accounts payable and receivable, bank reconciliation, online banking, billing and invoicing, sales tax management, expense tracking and financial reports. Striven says its construction tools capture labor hours and material and equipment costs at the source to show project profitability and cost overruns, and that budgets can be tracked down to individual expense and revenue items. For service trades, it describes scheduling that matches technicians' skills and availability to jobs, including emergency calls, plus parts inventory with restocking, fleet tracking, and tracking of subcontractor qualifications and documents. Projects can be viewed as Kanban boards, Gantt charts or lists, with project budgets and profitability reports.

Payroll is not part of the platform: Striven says it integrates with your preferred payroll provider. Staff can log time by hourly rate or service item from desktop or mobile, request time off and submit expenses. Striven says its support (chat, ticket submission and how-to questions) is free, and it offers implementation guides, videos and webinars.

The trade-off: Striven can replace QuickBooks plus separate scheduling and CRM tools, but per-user pricing ($35 or $70 a user, plus $25 a user under five users) adds up for a crew, payroll needs an outside provider, and a system that covers this many functions needs real setup work.
software.how_it_works: Striven is an online platform with mobile-friendly access for crews. Customers, vendors, items, projects and employees live in one database: project budgets are set up front, and labor, material and equipment costs recorded against a job flow into the built-in general ledger. The office schedules technicians, tracks parts and vehicles, and invoices from the same system, and customers and vendors can use portals (free up to 100 each). Payroll runs through an outside provider that Striven integrates with. Striven positions itself as a replacement for QuickBooks rather than an add-on to it. Pricing is per user per month.

pros_detail.title: Built-in accounting
pros_detail.explanation: General ledger, AP and AR, bank reconciliation, sales tax and financial reports live in the same system as your jobs, so costs don't have to be synced to separate books.

pros_detail.title: Job cost and budget tracking
pros_detail.explanation: Striven says it captures labor, material and equipment costs at the source and compares them with budgets to show project profitability.

pros_detail.title: Field service tools included
pros_detail.explanation: Technician scheduling (including emergency calls), parts inventory with restocking, fleet tracking and subcontractor document tracking are part of the platform.

pros_detail.title: Trade-specific solution pages
pros_detail.explanation: Striven has industry pages for HVAC, plumbing, electrical contracting, landscaping, construction and other field services.

pros_detail.title: Free support and training
pros_detail.explanation: Chat and ticket support, implementation guides, videos and webinars come at no extra charge, per Striven.

cons_detail.title: Per-user cost adds up

software.name: Melio
software.tagline: Bill pay that syncs to your books: pay subs and suppliers by ACH, card, check or wire from one place
software.pricing_summary: Go $0/mo (1 user, 5 free ACH payments a month, up to 10 QuickBooks/Xero syncs) · Core $25/mo ($20 billed annually; 20 free ACH a month; +$10/user) · Boost $55/mo ($44 annually; 50 free ACH a month; adds QuickBooks Desktop sync) · Unlimited $80/mo ($64 annually; unlimited free ACH and users; adds NetSuite sync) · Platinum custom. Fees: ACH $0.50 beyond the free ones, paper check $1.50, card payment 2.9%, same-day ACH or instant transfer 1% (max $75), wire $10.
software.headquartered: New York, NY (owned by Xero since October 2025)
software.long_description:
Melio is bill-pay (accounts payable) software for US small businesses, not full accounting. It pays vendors, subs and suppliers by ACH, card, paper check or wire, then syncs the payments to QuickBooks, Xero or NetSuite depending on the plan. Melio Payments Inc. is based in New York, and the Better Business Bureau lists it as started in March 2018. Xero completed its purchase of Melio on October 15, 2025, for US$2.5 billion upfront plus up to US$0.5 billion in contingent payments; Melio says it keeps operating independently and continues to support QuickBooks Online and QuickBooks Desktop users.

For trades, the useful part is paying every vendor from one place and choosing how to fund each payment. The free Go plan includes 5 ACH payments a month (each ACH after that is $0.50), and Melio mails a paper check for $1.50. Melio says you can pay a bill by card for a 2.9% fee even when the vendor doesn't accept cards, which can let you hold on to cash until your customer pays. Paid plans add more free ACH payments (20 on Core, 50 on Boost, unlimited on Unlimited), more users and custom approval workflows, and start with 90 days of unlimited free ACH.

Melio also covers basic receivables: you can create invoices and payment links, and customers pay free by bank transfer or by card with a 2.9% fee that either side can cover. The Better Business Bureau rates Melio Payments F, lists 102 complaints closed in the last three years, and shows it as not accredited, so read the BBB profile before relying on Melio for payments that can't be late.

The trade-off: Go is free but limited to one user, 5 free ACH payments a month and 10 accounting syncs; QuickBooks Desktop sync needs Boost ($55/mo) and NetSuite sync needs Unlimited ($80/mo); card payments cost 2.9%; and given the F rating from the BBB, keep a backup way to pay any bill that can't be late.
software.how_it_works: Add or forward a bill (Melio offers AI bill capture and a dedicated bills inbox), choose how and when to pay it (ACH from your bank, card, paper check or wire, including international payments), and Melio sends the payment. You can set auto-pay for recurring bills and, on paid plans, route payments through approval workflows before they go out. Payments sync to QuickBooks Online or Xero (up to 10 syncs on Go), QuickBooks Desktop from the Boost plan and NetSuite on Unlimited. For receivables, you create invoices or payment links that customers pay by bank transfer or card. Melio is not a general ledger, so you still need accounting software.

pros_detail.title: Free plan with 5 ACH payments a month
pros_detail.explanation: Go costs $0 for one user, with 5 free ACH payments a month and $0.50 per ACH after that.

pros_detail.title: Pays check-only vendors
pros_detail.explanation: Melio mails a paper check for $1.50, so suppliers who only take checks can be paid from the same place.

pros_detail.title: Pay by card even where cards aren't accepted
pros_detail.explanation: Melio says you can pay any bill by card for a 2.9% fee, even when the vendor doesn't take cards.

pros_detail.title: Syncs with your books
pros_detail.explanation: QuickBooks Online and Xero sync on paid plans (up to 10 syncs on Go), QuickBooks Desktop from Boost and NetSuite on Unlimited.

pros_detail.title: Approval workflows on paid plans
pros_detail.explanation: Core and up add users and custom approval workflows, so an owner can sign off on payments the office queues.

cons_detail.title: BBB rating of F
cons_detail.explanation: The Better Business Bureau rates Melio Payments F with 102 complaints closed in three years; keep a backup payment method for time-critical bills.

cons_detail.title: Not full accounting
cons_detail.explanation: Melio is bill pay and simple invoicing only; you still need QuickBooks, Xero or similar as your books.

cons_detail.explanation: Paying a large supplier invoice by card costs 2.9%, which adds up on big material orders.

cons_detail.explanation: Go allows one user, 5 free ACH payments a month and 10 accounting syncs; more users and approvals need a paid plan.

cons_detail.title: Some syncs need pricier plans
cons_detail.explanation: QuickBooks Desktop sync starts at Boost ($55/mo) and NetSuite sync needs Unlimited ($80/mo).

software.best_for: Small US contractors (GC, electrical, plumbing, HVAC, landscaping) who pay subs and suppliers and want low-cost bill pay that syncs to QuickBooks or Xero, with a backup for time-critical payments
software.weaknesses: BBB rates Melio Payments F (102 complaints closed in three years); not full accounting; 2.9% card fee; the free plan is limited to one user, 5 free ACH payments a month and 10 syncs; QuickBooks Desktop and NetSuite sync need the $55 and $80/mo plans
software.reputation_flag: The Better Business Bureau rates Melio Payments F and lists 102 complaints closed in the last three years, as of September 2026. It is not BBB accredited; read the BBB profile for details and keep a backup way to pay any bill that can't be late.

ratings.reddit_sentiment: liked for free ACH bill-pay and QuickBooks/Xero sync, but with a recurring and serious complaint pattern around sudden account freezes and held payments

software.affiliate_program: Yes: Melio Affiliate Program via PartnerStack (reported ~$300 per referred business / ~$600 per referred accounting firm client, 90-day cookie)
software.affiliate_payout_note: affiliate_url stays TBD until the PartnerStack tracking link and exact payout are confirmed

faqs.q: Is Melio accounting software?
faqs.a: No. Melio is bill pay (accounts payable) with simple invoicing, not a general ledger. It pays your vendors and subs by ACH, check, card or wire and syncs those payments to QuickBooks Online, QuickBooks Desktop, Xero or NetSuite depending on your plan, but you still need accounting software as your books.

faqs.q: How does Melio make bill pay free?
faqs.a: The Go plan is $0 for one user and includes 5 free ACH payments a month; each ACH after that is $0.50. Melio charges for other options: 2.9% to pay by card, $1.50 per mailed check, $10 per wire, and 1% (up to $75) for same-day ACH or instant transfers. Paid plans from $25/mo include more free ACH payments.

faqs.q: Is Melio safe to rely on?
faqs.a: Melio is owned by Xero, which completed its purchase on October 15, 2025, and Melio says it handles payments for hundreds of thousands of US businesses. The Better Business Bureau rates Melio Payments F and lists 102 complaints closed in the last three years, so read the BBB profile and keep a backup payment method for bills that can't be late.

faqs.q: Can Melio pay a supplier who only takes checks?
faqs.a: Yes. You schedule the payment in Melio and it mails a paper check to the vendor for $1.50 (a fast check is $20). You can pay every vendor from one place however each one wants to be paid.
